To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an existence theory for Abreu metrics on toric varieties, and we have proved a general result that relates the M-condition and injectivity radius.
we have obtained a general existence theory for solutions to the Abreu equation on compact toric manifolds with boundary, under the hypothesis that the “M-condition” holds.

(i) there exist smooth toric surfaces on which there is no extremal metric; (ii) there exist smooth, compact Kähler manifolds with positive Ricci curvature on which there is an extremal metric; and (iii) there exists a smooth, compact K\"ahler manifold with positive Ricci curvature on which there is not a unique extremal metric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the existence theory for solutions to the Abreu equation and the relationship of these solutions to extremal metrics on compact toric surfaces.
the existence theory of extremal metrics.
a continuity method approach for the existence of solutions to the Abreu equations on compact Kähler manifolds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Abreu equation is a powerful tool to construct new examples of Kähler metrics with special properties.
, for a given compact toric manifold M, the existence theory for extremal metrics is completely solved in the case where the injectivity radius of M is positive.

, for any toric surface, the Abreu equation has a solution with prescribed Monge-Ampère volume form, provided the volume is sufficiently close to the standard one, and the solution satisfies a uniform M-condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prove existence of solutions for the Abreu equation on toric surfaces under the M-condition.
the M-condition is satisfied by the Kähler-Einstein metrics, and the existence of the latter is a consequence of our theory.
we have established a continuity method for the existence of solutions to the Abreu equations, and have shown how the solutions are related to the injective radius of the toric surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the M-condition is a necessary and sufficient condition for existence.
the existence of solutions of the Abreau equation is related to the existence of solutions to a related Monge-Ampere equation with a “blow-up term”.
the existence of extremal metrics can be established by a continuity method in the space of solutions of the Abreau equation, and that the M-condition can be verified in a large class of examples.
